definition: Nonresponse is a research limitation in which some of the people meant to provide study data do not respond or do not provide usable information. In social and educational research, it is treated as a methodological weakness because it can leave the evidence less complete.

reasons: The packet only mentions nonresponse as a limitation in the reviewed studies; it does not define the term as people failing to respond or provide usable data.

The packet mentions “nonresponse” as a limitation highlighted by MMAT findings, but it does not define nonresponse as participants failing to respond or failing to provide usable information.
The packet does not state that nonresponse is treated as a methodological weakness in social/educational research.
